That is why the dual appears in His saying "they two were separated," and the feminine is used in agreement with the meaning of the rope, since he does not mean the literal rope, but the covenant and affection that existed between their peoples.

The apparent meaning of this verse is that He created the earth, placed the firm mountains in it, and blessed it; then He brought the heaven into being from smoke and shaped it as seven heavens. Thus the creation of the earth precedes the creation of the heaven, and the spreading of the earth is distinct from its creation; it occurred after the creation of the heaven. It has been objected to this that placing the mountains in it, blessing it, and apportioning its sustenance cannot occur until the earth exists. His saying ﴿and He blessed in it and apportioned in it its sustenance﴾ is explained as the creation of trees, plants, and animals in it, which cannot happen until it has become spread out. Then He said after that: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾, which requires the creation of the heaven to be after the creation and spreading of the earth.

It has also been objected that His saying to the heaven and the earth: ﴿Come, willingly or unwillingly﴾, is a metaphor for their bringing into being. So if the bringing into being of the earth preceded that of the heaven, it would require the bringing into being of something already existing by His command to the earth to come into being, which is impossible. This objection has been stated.

Al-Wahidi, in al-Basit, quoted Muqatil as saying: Allah created the heaven before the earth, and he interpreted His saying ﴿Then He turned to the heaven, and it was smoke﴾ as meaning "before He created the earth," and he supplied "was" (kāna) in it, as in His saying: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his has stolen before﴾ [Yusuf: 77], meaning: "If he has stolen." End of quotation.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: then the estimate would be "then He was (had been) turned to," which combines two opposites, because thumma indicates lateness and kāna indicates earlier time, so combining them yields a contradiction. A parallel would be: "I struck Zayd today, then I struck 'Amr yesterday." Just as this is false, so too what has been mentioned, that is, the interpretation of "then it was that He had turned," is false. He said: "My preferred view is that the creation of the heaven is prior to the creation of the earth. The interpretation of the verse is that creation is not an expression for bringing into being and existence, as shown by His saying: ﴿The likeness of Jesus with Allah is as the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him: Be, and he is﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59]; and this is impossible, since one does not say 'Be!' to a thing that already exists. Rather, creation is an expression for decree, and in regard to Him, exalted is He, its ruling is that it will come into being. His decreeing it is equivalent to creating the earth in two days, and His decreeing that something will come into being in a certain period does not require its occurrence at that moment. Therefore it does not follow that bringing the earth into being precedes bringing the heaven into being." End of quotation.

What we say is this: the unbelievers were rebuked and reproached for their disbelief in the One from whom all these things came, without any chronological order. The "then" (thumma) indicates the order of reporting, not the order of time and delay. As if He said: "The One who told you that He created the earth, placed firm mountains upon it, blessed it, and apportioned its sustenance in it, then told you that He turned to the heaven, there is no implication of order in the verse." That is, the chronological order did not occur for it.

Since the creation of the heaven is more wondrous in power than the creation of the earth, He arranged the reporting of it with "then" (thumma), so it becomes like His saying: ﴿Then he was among those who believed﴾ [al-Balad: 17] after His saying: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾ [al-Balad: 11].

From the order of reporting is His saying: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book﴾ [al-An'am: 154] after His saying: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite﴾ [al-An'am: 151]. His saying ﴿So He said to it and to the earth﴾, after reporting what He reported, serves to depict the creation of the two in accordance with His will, like your saying: "Have you seen the one you praised, when you said: 'He is a learned and righteous man'? This is a depiction of what you praised him for and an explanation of it." 

Thus He reported that He created such-and-such, and this decree was a bringing into being that did not deviate from His will. What indicates that the intended purpose is the reporting of the occurrence of these things without chronological order is His saying in al-Ra'd: ﴿Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see﴾ [al-Ra'd: 2], and then after that: ﴿And He is the One who spread out the earth and placed in it firm mountains and rivers﴾ [al-Ra'd: 3]. The apparent meaning of the verse we are discussing is that the placing of the mountains and the apportioning of sustenance happened before the turning to the heaven and its creation. But the purpose in both verses is to report that these things came from Him, exalted is He, without any reference to chronological order. What is mentioned as limited to two days, four days, or six days is only the measure of that according to you, not that there was a time period when these things were brought into being.

﴿So He completed them as seven heavens﴾, that is, He made them and brought them into being, as in the saying of Ibn Abi Dhu'ayb:

"And upon them two coats of mail, which David
completed, or which Tubba' made as flowing mail."

"And upon this, (seven) was placed in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl). Al-Ḥawfī said: it is a second object, as though he had included the meaning of qaḍāhunna (decreed them) in the sense of ṣayyarahunna (made them), so that it takes two objects. Al-Zamakhsharī said: it may also be an obscure pronoun, ﴿seven heavens﴾ being in the accusative of specification (tamyīz). By his saying "obscure" he means that it does not refer back to the heaven, neither in terms of wording nor in terms of meaning, unlike the circumstantial qualifier or the second object, which refers back to the heaven in terms of meaning.

﴿And He inspired in each heaven its affair﴾. Mujāhid and Qatādah said: He inspired into its inhabitants and its populaces from among the angels, and into it, in itself, He inspired what Allah the Exalted willed of the matters that are its establishment and its good order. This was also said by al-Suddī and Qatādah: and of the matters that pertain to other than it, such as the mountains of hail and the like that are within it; and he attributed the affair to it insofar as it is within it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: He commanded it what He commanded within it, and arranged it, from the creation of the angels, the luminous bodies, and other things.

(And protection) means: and We made them a protection, guarding them from the stealing listeners by means of piercing flames. It is permissible that it be an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu) according to the meaning, as if he said: And We created the lamps as an adornment and as a protection, end of quote.

There is no need for this second estimation, and its strain, when the first is evident and easy: "that" is a reference to all that has been mentioned, i.e., He brought it into being by His power, might and knowledge."

Surat Fussilat has fifty-four verses and is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Ha Mim.﴾ ﴿A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾ ﴿A Book whose verses are made distinct, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know.﴾ ﴿Bearing good news and a warning, yet most of them turn away, so they do not listen.﴾ ﴿And they say: "Our hearts are under coverings against what you call us to, and there is deafness in our ears, and between us and you there is a barrier. So act, for we are acting."﴾ ﴿Say: "I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is one God. So go straight to Him and seek His forgiveness." And woe to the polytheists,﴾ ﴿who do not give the zakat and who disbelieve in the Hereafter.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that is never cut off.﴾ ﴿Say: "Do you really disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and do you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds."﴾ ﴿He placed in it firm mountains above it, blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance in four days, equally, for those who ask.﴾ ﴿Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and revealed in each heaven its command. We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as a protection. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿If they turn away, say: "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud."﴾ [Fussilat: 13] ﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and behind them, saying: "Worship none but Allah." They said: "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels. So we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ [Fussilat: 14] ﴿As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the earth without right, and they said: "Who is stronger than us in power?" Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is stronger than them in power? And they used to deny Our signs.﴾ [Fussilat: 15] ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind in ill-omened days, to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.﴾ [Fussilat: 16] ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance. So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them because of what they used to earn.﴾ [Fussilat: 17] ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to be godfearing.﴾ [Fussilat: 18] ﴿And on the day when the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in order.﴾ [Fussilat: 19] ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them about what they used to do.﴾ [Fussilat: 20] ﴿They will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?" They will say: "Allah has made us speak, the One who makes everything speak. He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned."﴾ [Fussilat: 21] ﴿You did not hide yourselves so that your hearing, your sight, and your skins would not testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ [Fussilat: 22] ﴿That was your opinion which you held about your Lord; it has ruined you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ [Fussilat: 23] ﴿If they endure, the Fire is their dwelling. And if they ask to be shown favour, they will not be among those granted it.﴾ [Fussilat: 24] ﴿We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and behind them. The word has come true against them, as it did against the nations that passed away before them, of jinn and humans. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ [Fussilat: 25] ﴿Those who disbelieve say: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it, so that you may prevail."﴾ [Fussilat: 26] ﴿So We will make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, and We will repay them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ [Fussilat: 27] ﴿That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, for them therein is the abode of eternity, as a recompense for their denying Our signs.﴾ [Fussilat: 28] ﴿Those who disbelieve say: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray, from the jinn and humans, and we will put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest."﴾ [Fussilat: 29] ﴿Indeed, those who say: "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them: "Do not fear and do not grieve, but rejoice in the Garden which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30] ﴿We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. For you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for.﴾ [Fussilat: 31] ﴿As a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful. And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says: "I am among the Muslims"?﴾ [Fussilat: 32] ﴿Good and evil are not equal. Repel evil with what is better, and then the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as if he were a devoted friend.﴾ [Fussilat: 34] ﴿None is granted this except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ [Fussilat: 35] ﴿And if a provocation from Satan provokes you, seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [Fussilat: 36] ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him that you worship.﴾ [Fussilat: 37] ﴿But if they are arrogant, those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they never tire.﴾ [Fussilat: 38] ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, the One who gave it life is the One who gives life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things capable.﴾ [Fussilat: 39] ﴿Indeed, those who distort Our signs are not hidden from Us. Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do what you wish; indeed, He sees what you do.﴾ [Fussilat: 40] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them. And indeed, it is a mighty Book.﴾ [Fussilat: 41] ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.﴾ [Fussilat: 42] ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is One of forgiveness and of painful punishment.﴾ [Fussilat: 43] ﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said: "Why are its verses not made clear? Is it non-Arabic while the messenger is Arab?" Say: "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. But for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. Those are called from a far place."﴾ [Fussilat: 44] (p. 481) ﴿And We gave Moses the Book, but it was disputed. Had a word from your Lord not preceded, the matter would have been decided between them. And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it.﴾ [Fussilat: 45] ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is against it. And your Lord is not unjust to the servants.﴾ [Fussilat: 46] ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. No fruit comes out of its sheaths, no female conceives or gives birth, except with His knowledge. On the day He calls to them: "Where are My partners?" they will say: "We inform You that none of us is a witness."﴾ [Fussilat: 47] ﴿And what they used to invoke before has strayed from them, and they will think that they have no place of refuge.﴾ [Fussilat: 48] ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is hopeless and despairing.﴾ [Fussilat: 49] ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some hardship has touched him, he will say: "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will come. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him." We will certainly inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will certainly make them taste a severe punishment.﴾ [Fussilat: 50] ﴿And when We bestow favour on man, he turns away and withdraws to one side, but when evil touches him, he has long prayers.﴾ [Fussilat: 51] ﴿Say: "Have you considered? If it is from Allah and you then disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?"﴾ [Fussilat: 52] ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient that your Lord is a witness over all things?﴾ [Fussilat: 53] ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about meeting their Lord. Unquestionably, He encompasses all things.﴾ [Fussilat: 54]

Al-Sarsar (the cold wind that burns as fire does), said al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj; the views of the exegetes on it will come.

Al-Nahs (ill-omened): the opposite of good fortune. The poet said:
"It is all the same to him at whatever time you come to him, whether it is an hour of ill-omen to be avoided or of good fortune."

al-Farra' recited:
"Tell Judham and Lakhm that their brothers, Tayy and Bahra', are a people whose help is ill-omened."

Al-Taqyid (pl. al-taqyid): the preparing and facilitating of a thing. "These are two garments of equal value (qayyidan)" when they are equal in price. "Qayidni with this garment" means: take it and give me in exchange its equivalent. Al-muqayada means exchange.

Al-akmam: its singular is kumm. al-Zamakhshari said it is with a kasra on the kaf. al-Mubarrad said it is what covers the fruit before the spathe dries. Whoever says in the plural akimma, its singular is kimam. Al-afaq (the horizons): the regions, its singular is ufuq. The poet said:
"Even if a living being attained, by a station in this world, the horizon of the sky, his hand would attain the horizon."

Ha Mim. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are made distinct... [The Qur'anic verses in this opening section are repeated in the source; they are rendered above.]

This surah is Meccan without disagreement. Its connection to what precedes it: He said at the end of the previous surah: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth?﴾ [Ghafir: 82] to the end. So it included a threat, a warning, and a rebuke to Quraysh. He then followed that rebuke, reproof, and threat with another reproof. He mentioned that He sent down a Book whose verses are detailed, a bearer of good news to whoever follows it and a warner to whoever turns away from it, and that most of Quraysh turned away from it.

Then He mentioned the power of God to create the upper and lower worlds. Then He said: ﴿If they turn away, say: "I have warned you of a thunderbolt"﴾ [Fussilat: 13]. All of this fits the end of Surat al-Mu'min regarding the non-benefit to the deniers of the messengers when punishment overtook them. Likewise, Quraysh suffered what befell its chieftains of killing, capture, plunder, and captivity, and the uprooting of the enemies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), similar to what befell 'Ad and Thamud of uprooting.

It is narrated that 'Utba ibn Rabi'a went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in order to magnify for him the matter of his opposition to his people, to disparage what he had brought, and to make it seem remote. When 'Utba spoke, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: Ha Mim, and went on with it at its beginning until he reached His saying: ﴿If they turn away, say: "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud."﴾ [Fussilat: 13]. The old man trembled and his hair stood on end. He put his hand over the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and appealed to him by the ties of kinship to stop. When he left him, he said: "By Allah, I have heard something that is neither poetry, nor sorcery, nor soothsaying. And I thought that the thunderbolt of punishment was over my head."

"Tanzil" (a revelation) is in the nominative because it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "This is a revelation," according to al-Farra'. Or it is the subject whose predicate is "a Book whose verses are made distinct," according to al-Zajjaj and al-Hawfi. The predicate of "Ha Mim" is if it is the name of the surah. "A Book" according to al-Zajjaj is an apposition to "tanzil." It was said: or a predicate after a predicate.

"Whose verses are made distinct": al-Suddi said: its verses were clarified, meaning its meanings were explained, so its lawful and unlawful, its prohibitions and commands, its promises and threats were differentiated.

It was said: it was made distinct in the revelation, meaning it was not sent down all at once. al-Hasan said: with promise and threat. Sufyan said: with reward and punishment. Ibn Zayd said: distinguishing between Muhammad (ﷺ) and whoever opposes him. It was said: it was made distinct by its sections and by the varieties of the endings of verses, and it did not follow a rhyme or the like, as poetry and rhymed prose do.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: its verses were distinguished and made into detailed meanings of different kinds. Some of them concern the description of the essence of Allah, the explanation of the attributes of transcendence and sanctity, the explanation of the perfection of His knowledge, power, mercy, and wisdom, and the wonders of the states of His creation: the heavens, the stars, the alternation of night and day, and the wonders of the states of plants, animals, and humans. Some of them concern the states of obligations directed toward the heart and toward the limbs. Some concern promise and threat, reward and punishment, and the ranks of the people of Paradise and the depths of the people of Hell. Some concern admonitions and advice. Some concern the refinement of morals and the discipline of the soul. Some concern the stories of earlier peoples and the histories of those who passed away.

Ultimately, whoever is fair will know that at the beginning of creation there was no book that gathered together the diverse sciences and subjects as the Qur'an does. End of quotation.

It is also recited as (fa-ṣalat), with the fa vowelled and the ṣad light (mukhaffafa), meaning: it distinguished between truth and falsehood; or some of its parts were distinguished from others by the difference of its meanings, from the verse ﴿فَصَلَتِ العِيرُ﴾ [Yusuf: 94], i.e., departed (infaṣalat), and "faṣala min al-balad," i.e., he departed from the town. (Qur'anan) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl) in itself, and it is emphatic (mu'akkida), because it does not change; or it is a preparation (tawṭi'a) for the state after it, which is (ʿarabiyyan); or it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar), i.e., he recites it as an Arabic Qur'an; or it is in the accusative for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) and praise (madḥ).

As for the one who makes it a state, it is said that the one in state is (āyātuhu), and it is said (kitāb), because it is described by the words ﴿فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ﴾; or by supposing a hidden verb whose estimate is: "We distinguished it as a Qur'an"; or it is a second object of (fuṣṣilat). These are six opinions, the last of which belongs to al-Akhfash. (Li-qawmin) is connected to (fuṣṣilat), i.e., they know things and understand the proofs, so it is as if it was distinguished for these people, since they benefit from it; they are singled out for mention as an honour. Whoever does not benefit from the distinction is as if it was not distinguished for him. It is unlikely that it is connected to (tanzīl), because it has been described in one of its two connections, if ﴿مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ is in the position of a description, or (kitāb) is substituted from it, or it is the predicate of (tanzīl), in which case there would be a substitution from the relative pronoun and an information about it before it takes its connection, and this is not permissible. It is also said that (li-qawmin) is in the position of a description of (ʿarabiyyan), i.e., existing for a people who know its words and verify that it has not departed from the pattern of their speech; and this is as if it were a refutation of those who claim that there is in the Qur'an what is not from the speech of the Arabs. (Bashīran wa-nadhīran) is in the accusative as a description of ﴿قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾. It is also said it is a state from (āyātuhu). Zayd ibn ʿAlī recited ﴿بَشِيرٌ ونَذِيرٌ﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 19] with both in the nominative, as a description of (kitāb), or as the predicate of an omitted subject. Its good tidings are of Paradise for whoever believes, and its warning is of the Fire for whoever disbelieves.

﴿فَأعْرَضَ أكْثَرُهُمْ﴾: i.e., most of those people; that is, they were among the people of knowledge, but they did not consider it with complete reflection; rather they turned away. ﴿فَهم لا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾: because of their turning away from what it contains of proofs and evidences; or, since it did not benefit them and they did not accept it, they were treated as if they had not heard it.

Then God, exalted is He, informed about them with the statement that indicates the impossibility of their hearts (returning) and of people returning to Him, and of their hearing what follows it; and it is His saying, exalted is He, quoting them: ﴿وقالُوا قُلُوبُنا في أكِنَّةٍ مِمّا تَدْعُونا إلَيْهِ وفي آذانِنا وقْرٌ﴾. The discussion of the like of this has already passed in al-An'am.

Ṭalḥa recited (wiqr) with a kasra on the waw. These are images of the impossibility of accepting the truth, as if their hearts were in a covering, as they said: ﴿وقالُوا قُلُوبُنا غُلْفٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 88], and as if their ears, when the speech of God is mentioned, were deaf. The (ḥijāb) is the veil that prevents response, and it is a difference in religion, because he worships God while they worship idols; this is the meaning stated by al-Farra' and others.

It is narrated that Abu Jahl wrapped a garment over his head and said: "O Muhammad, between us and you is a veil," mocking him. It is said it is an image of non-response. It is said it is an expression for enmity. The (min) in ﴿مِمّا تَدْعُونا إلَيْهِ﴾ is for the beginning of the limit, and likewise in ﴿ومِن بَيْنِنا﴾. The meaning is that the veil began from us and began from you, so the intermediate distance between our direction and your direction is filled with the veil, with no empty space in it. Had he not used (min), the meaning would be that a veil exists midway between the two directions; and the intent is to emphasise extreme separation, which is why (min) was used.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you say: why was it not said, 'upon our hearts are coverings,' as it was said, 'and in our ears is deafness,' so that the speech would be in one pattern?" (I say): It is in one pattern, because there is no difference in meaning between your saying "our hearts are in coverings," and the proof of this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. If it were said, "We have made their hearts in coverings," the meaning would not differ. You see that the obedient ones among them do not observe correspondence and considered metaphor except in meanings, and you say that (fī) is more eloquent in this position than (ʿalā), because they intended the extreme of non-acceptance, since their hearts are in coverings which enclose them in the way a container encloses what is in it, so nothing can reach them. Just as you say: "the money is in the bag," in contrast to "upon the money is a bag," which does not indicate confinement and non-attainment in the way a container does. As for His saying, "We have made," it is information from God, exalted is He, and needs no exaggeration, unlike their saying.

Al-Zamakhshari's saying "you see the obedient ones" means among the Arabs and their poets. For this reason people spoke about the poetry of Habib, and some did not approve of the excessive craft of badi' in it; they said: the best of it is what comes without artifice.

﴿فاعْمَلْ إنَّنا عامِلُونَ﴾. Al-Kalbi said: "Work for our destruction, for we are working for your destruction."

Muqatil said: "Work for your god who sent you, for we are working for our gods whom we worship." Al-Farra' said: "Work according to the requirement of your religion, and we work according to the requirement of our religion." Al-Mawardi mentioned: "Work for your afterlife, for we work for our worldly life."

Since the heart is the locus of knowledge, and hearing and sight are aids in acquiring knowledge, they mentioned that these three are veiled from anything that the Messenger brings reaching them. The saying "So work, for we are working" may mean: you will be wholly abandoned, and it may be contemptuous mockery.

(Qul innamā yūḥā ilayya): The majority recited (qul) in the imperative; Ibn Wathhab and al-A'mash recited (qāla) as a past verb. This is a proclamation of monotheism and prophethood. Al-Nakha'i and al-A'mash recited (yūḥī) with a kasra on the ḥā'; the majority with a fatḥa. He informed that he is a human like them, not an angel, but it was revealed to him rather than to them.

Al-Hasan said: God taught him humility, and that what was revealed to him was the oneness of God and the rejection of your gods.

﴿فاسْتَقِيمُوا إلَيْهِ﴾: i.e., go straight toward Him with monotheism, which is the foundation of religion and of action. ﴿واسْتَغْفِرُوهُ﴾: ask Him for forgiveness, for it is the foundation of action, by whose attainment consequences are removed.

(Istaqīmū) has been given the meaning of turning, which is why it takes (ilā); i.e., direct your uprightness toward Him. Since reason affirms that happiness is tied to two matters: exalting God and compassion toward His creation, He mentioned that woe, perdition and grief are for the polytheists who did not exalt God in His monotheism and the denial of a partner, and did not show compassion to His creation by bringing good to them; and in addition to this they denied resurrection.

The apparent meaning is that (zakāt) is in its literal sense of the zakāt of wealth; this was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib, who said: they used to perform Hajj and ʿUmra but did not pay zakāt. Al-Hasan and Qatada said, and it was said: Quraysh used to feed pilgrims and deprive those among them who believed.

Al-Hasan and Qatada also said: the meaning is that they do not believe in zakāt and do not acknowledge it.

Mujahid and al-Rabi' said: they do not purify their deeds. Ibn ʿAbbas and the majority said: zakāt here is "There is no god but God," monotheism, as Musa, peace be upon him, said to Pharaoh: ﴿هَلْ لَكَ إلى أنْ تَزَكّى﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 18]. What supports this interpretation is that the verse is from the early Meccan period, and the zakāt of wealth was revealed in Medina; this was said by Ibn ʿAtiyya, who said: this is only the zakāt of the heart and body, i.e., purification from polytheism and sins; and Mujahid and al-Rabi' said the same.

Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: zakāt here is spending in obedience. End of quotation.

If the zakāt intended is the giving of wealth, then it was linked with disbelief because it is burdensome to give away wealth, which is beloved to human nature and the brother of the soul, as an incitement to it. A certain man of letters said:

They said: "The soul's brother is your wealth, so guard it." I replied: "Wealth is better than the soul."
I see that guarding it leads to the improvement of my condition, and squandering it leads to a shameful begging.

﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning the sick and the infirm who are unable to complete acts of obedience; for them is written a reward like the best of what they used to do. (Mamnūn) means diminished; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with him. Dhu al-Asbagh al-ʿAdwani said:

By your life, my door is not locked against a friend, nor is my goodness diminished.

Mujahid said: "not counted." It is also said: "not cut off." The poet said:

The bounty of the generous over the slow horses; he gives in that way neither diminished nor hasty.

It is also said: he does not reproach with it, because God's gifts are an honour, whereas reproach only enters human gifts. It is also said: he does not reproach with it, because it is only a reproach of favour; as for the other (the reward), it is a right whose payment is owed. Al-Zamakhshari transmitted this, and in it there is a hint of Mu'tazilite doctrine.

﴿قُلْ أئِنَّكم لَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾: a question of rebuke and reproach against them, for disbelieving in the One who brought into being the world, its lower and upper parts, and described the form of its creation and its duration; and the wisdom in creating over a period of time while He is capable of bringing it into being all at once.

So God mentioned the bringing into being of these things in sequence, and the discussion of what was first begun in creation and what was created in sequence has already passed.

The meaning of ﴿فِي يَوْمَيْنِ﴾ is: within the measure of two days.

﴿وتَجْعَلُونَ لَهُ أنْدادًا﴾: i.e., likenesses and equals from among the angels, the jinn and the idols, which they worship besides Him. al-Suddi said: equals among men whom they obey.

(Wa-tajʿalūna) is conjoined to ﴿لَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾, so it falls within the scope of the interrogation that implies denial and rebuke. (Dhālika): i.e., the Originator of the earth and its Inventor, ﴿رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾, is (distinct) from the equals you have set up for Him and others.

﴿وجَعَلَ فِيها رَواسِيَ﴾: a new statement, not part of the relative clause at all; rather it is conjoined to His saying ﴿لَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾.

﴿وبارَكَ فِيها﴾: He multiplied its good within it.

﴿وقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها﴾: i.e., the provisions of its inhabitants and their livelihoods; and He attributed both to the earth in terms of their being in it and emerging from it; this was said by al-Suddi.

Qatada said: "its sustenance" means from the mountains, rivers, trees, rocks, minerals, and the things by which the earth's stability and benefits subsist.

Mujahid said: "its sustenance" means from the rain and waters. ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak and Mujahid also said: its specific properties which He distributed among the lands, by which each region is distinguished, so that some of them need others for sustenance through clothing, food and plants.

﴿فِي أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ﴾: i.e., in the full completion of four days, together with the two days mentioned earlier. Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿فِي أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ﴾ is for the duration of God's creation and what is in it, as if He said: all of that was in four complete days, equal, without addition or subtraction.

Al-Zajjaj said: "in completion of four days," meaning by the completion the two days. End of quotation. This is like saying: "I built the wall of my house in one day, and completed all of it in two days," meaning with the first.

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Razi said: From al-Zamakhshari's words one understands an additional benefit in ﴿فِي أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ﴾ beyond His saying "in two days," because "in two days" does not imply that the work was entirely occupied with that. But when He mentioned the creation of the earth and the creation of these things, then said ﴿فِي أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ سَواءً﴾, this indicates that these days were fully occupied with those works without addition or subtraction. End of quotation.

﴿in four days﴾ is not different from ﴿two days and four days﴾ in terms of encompassing (istighraq, the sense of covering the whole span). If ﴿four﴾ implies encompassing, then so do the two days. When a counted time-span is mentioned, the verb applies to all of it, either generally, as in "I traveled two days," or to part of each day, as in "I prayed at night for two nights." Encompassing is therefore possible, and so is partial occurrence within each of the two nights. In the same way, the creation of the earth could have occurred during part of each of the two days, or the two days could have been wholly devoted to it. Likewise, ﴿in four days﴾ allows for encompassing, and the creation of the earth, the mountains, the blessing, and the apportioning of its sustenance could have occurred during part of each of the four days [p-486]. Thus, what Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said adds no further benefit.

Al-Jumhur read (سَواءً) with the accusative (naṣb) as a circumstantial state (ḥāl). Abu Ja'far read it with the nominative (raf'), meaning "it is equal." Zayd ibn 'Ali, al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd, 'Isa, and Ya'qub read it with the genitive (khafḍ), as an adjective (na't) of ﴿four days﴾.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: its meaning is (سَواءً) "equally" for the one who asks about the matter, who inquires about the reality of its occurrence and seeks the lesson in it; he will find it as Allah, exalted is He, said.

Ibn Zayd and a group said: its meaning is that the affair of these creatures is ready and arranged, and their benefit is available to the people who need them. He used the word "those who ask" to mean "those who seek," because seeking what benefits them is part of their nature, since they are in a state of need.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: with what is the phrase ﴿for those who ask﴾ connected? I say: with an omitted element, as if it were said: this enumeration is for the sake of the one who asks how long the earth and what is in it took to create; or [it is connected to a verb understood as] 'He apportioned in it its sustenance' for the sake of those who seek it, the needy who live on it." End of quotation. This returns to the view of the earlier exegetes.

When he explained the creation of the earth and what is in it, he followed it with the creation of the heaven, saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾, that is, He intended it and directed Himself to it without intending to influence anything else. The meaning is: toward the creation of the heaven. The apparent meaning is that the material from which the heaven was created was smoke.

At the beginning of the book which the Jews claim is the Torah, it is said that His throne, exalted is He, was upon the water before the creation of the heavens and the earth. Then Allah produced heat in that, and foam and smoke rose up. The foam remained on the surface of the water, and from it Allah created dryness and produced the earth from it; the smoke rose up and went back, and from it Allah created the heavens. In the same text it is also said that He created the heaven from dark parts. End of quotation.

It has also been narrated that it was a soft body, like smoke or vapor. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: here there is an omitted word indicated by the apparent sense, and its estimate is: so He brought it into being, perfected it, and completed its affairs; and then ﴿He said to it and to the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly﴾. He preferred the view of those who held that the two actually spoke, and that Allah gave them life and perception that required their speech. After mentioning that some exegetes held that this is figurative, and that obedience, submission, and humility appeared from them in a manner equivalent to speech, he said: "The first view is better, because nothing repels it, its lesson is more complete, and its power is more evident." End of quotation.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "What is meant by commanding the heaven and the earth to come is that He willed their existence, and their compliance is that they did not resist Him; they came into being as He willed, and they came as an obedient subject does when the command of the one who commands reaches him. Or it is that Allah, exalted is He, spoke to the heaven and the earth and said to them: ﴿Come﴾, whether you wish it or not. They said: ﴿We come willingly, not unwillingly.﴾ The purpose is to depict the effect of His power on what is subject to it, and nothing else, without establishing any actual speech or reply. A similar statement is the saying of the speaker: 'The wall said to the peg: Why do you split me? The peg said: Ask the one who hammers me.' Then he did not leave me behind the stone that is behind me." 

"If you ask: why did He mention the heaven together with the earth and join them in the command to come, when the earth was created two days before the heaven? I say: He first created the body of the earth without spreading it out, then after the creation of the heaven He spread it out, as He said: ﴿And the earth after that He spread out﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 30]. So the meaning is: come in the form that you should come in, in terms of shape and description: come, O earth, spread out as a resting place and a cradle for your people; and come, O heaven, vaulted as a roof over them." The meaning of coming (al-itya') is occurrence and taking place, as one says: "his deed came accepted and pleasing." It is also possible that the meaning is: let each of them come to the other with the coming that is intended and required by wisdom and planning, such as the earth being a resting place for the heaven, and the heaven being a roof for the earth. This is supported by the reading of those who read (أتَيا) and (أتَيْنا) from al-muwatah, which means agreement, that is: let each of them agree with its sister and be in accord with her. They said: "We agreed and assisted." It also allows the meaning: agree with My command and My will, and do not resist.

"If you ask: what is the meaning of 'willingly or unwillingly'? I say: it is a figure of speech for the necessity of the effect of His power upon them, and that their resistance to the effect of His power is impossible, just as the tyrant says to one whom he wishes to test: 'You will do this whether you want to or not, and you will do it willingly or unwillingly.'"

[p-487] Their being in the accusative is as a circumstantial state, meaning "willing" or "unwilling." "If you ask: why was it not said 'willing' (ṭā'i'atayn) in agreement with the wording, or 'willing' (ṭā'i'atān) in agreement with the meaning, since they are heavens and earths? I say: when they were treated as addressees and respondents, and described with willingness and unwillingness, it was said 'obedient ones' (ṭā'i'īn) in place of 'obedient females,' like His saying 'prostrating ones' (sājidīn)." End of quotation.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿come﴾ (ā'tiyā) from the verb to come, meaning: come to My command and My will. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Mujahid read (أتَيا) on the pattern faʿalā, and ﴿they said: we came﴾ (أتَيْنا) on the pattern faʿalnā, from ātā yu'tī. Thus Ibn 'Atiyyah said, and he said: this means "give" from yourselves the obedience that I desire from you. All of this refers to their subjection and what Allah decreed of their functions. End of quotation.

It was mentioned earlier in al-Zamakhshari's words that he took this reading to be from al-muwatah, meaning agreement. On this view the pattern of ātiyā is fā'ila and ātaynā is fā'alnā. Abu al-Fadl al-Razi preceded him in this, saying: "ātaynā with the long vowel is on the pattern fā'alnā from al-muwatah, and its meaning is 'we hastened,' with the object omitted. It cannot be from al-itā' (giving), which is 'bestowing,' because its object would be too far removed." End of quotation.

Al-A'mash read (كُرْهًا) with a damma on the kaf. The more correct view is that it is a dialectal variant of (كَرْهًا) meaning compulsion to do something which is offered as a choice between it and willing compliance. The more common view is that (كُرْه) with a damma means hardship.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: his saying ﴿they said﴾ intends the two groups mentioned: He made the heavens into one heaven and the earths into one earth. This is like the saying of the poet:

"Did it not grieve you that the ropes of my people
and your people have been severed in separation?"

and He expressed it with ﴿they two were separated﴾. End of quotation.

This is not as stated. The earth was mentioned only in the singular, and the heaven is singular, but they are referred to in the dual for the sake of graceful expression. The verse is an instance of using the plural in place of the dual; it is as if he said: "Did it not grieve you that the two ropes of my people and your people...?" That is why the dual appears in His saying "they two were separated," and the feminine is used in agreement with the meaning of the rope, since he does not mean the literal rope, but the covenant and affection that existed between their peoples.

The apparent meaning of this verse is that He created the earth, placed the firm mountains in it, and blessed it; then He brought the heaven into being from smoke and shaped it as seven heavens. Thus the creation of the earth precedes the creation of the heaven, and the spreading of the earth is distinct from its creation; it occurred after the creation of the heaven. It has been objected to this that placing the mountains in it, blessing it, and apportioning its sustenance cannot occur until the earth exists. His saying ﴿and He blessed in it and apportioned in it its sustenance﴾ is explained as the creation of trees, plants, and animals in it, which cannot happen until it has become spread out. Then He said after that: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾, which requires the creation of the heaven to be after the creation and spreading of the earth.

It has also been objected that His saying to the heaven and the earth: ﴿Come, willingly or unwillingly﴾, is a metaphor for their bringing into being. So if the bringing into being of the earth preceded that of the heaven, it would require the bringing into being of something already existing by His command to the earth to come into being, which is impossible. This objection has been stated.

Al-Wahidi, in al-Basit, quoted Muqatil as saying: Allah created the heaven before the earth, and he interpreted His saying ﴿Then He turned to the heaven, and it was smoke﴾ as meaning "before He created the earth," and he supplied "was" (kāna) in it, as in His saying: ﴿If he steals, a brother of his has stolen before﴾ [Yusuf: 77], meaning: "If he has stolen." End of quotation.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: then the estimate would be "then He was (had been) turned to," which combines two opposites, because thumma indicates lateness and kāna indicates earlier time, so combining them yields a contradiction. A parallel would be: "I struck Zayd today, then I struck 'Amr yesterday." Just as this is false, so too what has been mentioned, that is, the interpretation of "then it was that He had turned," is false. He said: "My preferred view is that the creation of the heaven is prior to the creation of the earth. The interpretation of the verse is that creation is not an expression for bringing into being and existence, as shown by His saying: ﴿The likeness of Jesus with Allah is as the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him: Be, and he is﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59]; and this is impossible, since one does not say 'Be!' to a thing that already exists. Rather, creation is an expression for decree, and in regard to Him, exalted is He, its ruling is that it will come into being. His decreeing it is equivalent to creating the earth in two days, and His decreeing that something will come into being in a certain period does not require its occurrence at that moment. Therefore it does not follow that bringing the earth into being precedes bringing the heaven into being." End of quotation.

What we say is this: the unbelievers were rebuked and reproached for their disbelief in the One from whom all these things came, without any chronological order. The "then" (thumma) indicates the order of reporting, not the order of time and delay. As if He said: "The One who told you that He created the earth, placed firm mountains upon it, blessed it, and apportioned its sustenance in it, then told you that He turned to the heaven, there is no implication of order in the verse." That is, the chronological order did not occur for it.

Since the creation of the heaven is more wondrous in power than the creation of the earth, He arranged the reporting of it with "then" (thumma), so it becomes like His saying: ﴿Then he was among those who believed﴾ [al-Balad: 17] after His saying: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾ [al-Balad: 11].

From the order of reporting is His saying: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book﴾ [al-An'am: 154] after His saying: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite﴾ [al-An'am: 151]. His saying ﴿So He said to it and to the earth﴾, after reporting what He reported, serves to depict the creation of the two in accordance with His will, like your saying: "Have you seen the one you praised, when you said: 'He is a learned and righteous man'? This is a depiction of what you praised him for and an explanation of it." 

Thus He reported that He created such-and-such, and this decree was a bringing into being that did not deviate from His will. What indicates that the intended purpose is the reporting of the occurrence of these things without chronological order is His saying in al-Ra'd: ﴿Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see﴾ [al-Ra'd: 2], and then after that: ﴿And He is the One who spread out the earth and placed in it firm mountains and rivers﴾ [al-Ra'd: 3]. The apparent meaning of the verse we are discussing is that the placing of the mountains and the apportioning of sustenance happened before the turning to the heaven and its creation. But the purpose in both verses is to report that these things came from Him, exalted is He, without any reference to chronological order. What is mentioned as limited to two days, four days, or six days is only the measure of that according to you, not that there was a time period when these things were brought into being.

﴿So He completed them as seven heavens﴾, that is, He made them and brought them into being, as in the saying of Ibn Abi Dhu'ayb:

"And upon them two coats of mail, which David
completed, or which Tubba' made as flowing mail."

"And upon this, (seven) was placed in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl). Al-Ḥawfī said: it is a second object, as though he had included the meaning of qaḍāhunna (decreed them) in the sense of ṣayyarahunna (made them), so that it takes two objects. Al-Zamakhsharī said: it may also be an obscure pronoun, ﴿seven heavens﴾ being in the accusative of specification (tamyīz). By his saying "obscure" he means that it does not refer back to the heaven, neither in terms of wording nor in terms of meaning, unlike the circumstantial qualifier or the second object, which refers back to the heaven in terms of meaning.

﴿And He inspired in each heaven its affair﴾. Mujāhid and Qatādah said: He inspired into its inhabitants and its populaces from among the angels, and into it, in itself, He inspired what Allah the Exalted willed of the matters that are its establishment and its good order. This was also said by al-Suddī and Qatādah: and of the matters that pertain to other than it, such as the mountains of hail and the like that are within it; and he attributed the affair to it insofar as it is within it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: He commanded it what He commanded within it, and arranged it, from the creation of the angels, the luminous bodies, and other things.

(And protection) means: and We made them a protection, guarding them from the stealing listeners by means of piercing flames. It is permissible that it be an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu) according to the meaning, as if he said: And We created the lamps as an adornment and as a protection, end of quote.

There is no need for this second estimation, and its strain, when the first is evident and easy: "that" is a reference to all that has been mentioned, i.e., He brought it into being by His power, might and knowledge."

Surat Fussilat has fifty-four verses and is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Ha Mim.﴾ ﴿A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾ ﴿A Book whose verses are made distinct, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know.﴾ ﴿Bearing good news and a warning, yet most of them turn away, so they do not listen.﴾ ﴿And they say: "Our hearts are under coverings against what you call us to, and there is deafness in our ears, and between us and you there is a barrier. So act, for we are acting."﴾ ﴿Say: "I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is one God. So go straight to Him and seek His forgiveness." And woe to the polytheists,﴾ ﴿who do not give the zakat and who disbelieve in the Hereafter.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that is never cut off.﴾ ﴿Say: "Do you really disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and do you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds."﴾ ﴿He placed in it firm mountains above it, blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance in four days, equally, for those who ask.﴾ ﴿Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and revealed in each heaven its command. We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as a protection. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿If they turn away, say: "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud."﴾ [Fussilat: 13] ﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and behind them, saying: "Worship none but Allah." They said: "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels. So we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ [Fussilat: 14] ﴿As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the earth without right, and they said: "Who is stronger than us in power?" Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is stronger than them in power? And they used to deny Our signs.﴾ [Fussilat: 15] ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind in ill-omened days, to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.﴾ [Fussilat: 16] ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance. So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them because of what they used to earn.﴾ [Fussilat: 17] ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to be godfearing.﴾ [Fussilat: 18] ﴿And on the day when the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in order.﴾ [Fussilat: 19] ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them about what they used to do.﴾ [Fussilat: 20] ﴿They will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?" They will say: "Allah has made us speak, the One who makes everything speak. He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned."﴾ [Fussilat: 21] ﴿You did not hide yourselves so that your hearing, your sight, and your skins would not testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ [Fussilat: 22] ﴿That was your opinion which you held about your Lord; it has ruined you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ [Fussilat: 23] ﴿If they endure, the Fire is their dwelling. And if they ask to be shown favour, they will not be among those granted it.﴾ [Fussilat: 24] ﴿We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and behind them. The word has come true against them, as it did against the nations that passed away before them, of jinn and humans. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ [Fussilat: 25] ﴿Those who disbelieve say: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it, so that you may prevail."﴾ [Fussilat: 26] ﴿So We will make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, and We will repay them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ [Fussilat: 27] ﴿That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, for them therein is the abode of eternity, as a recompense for their denying Our signs.﴾ [Fussilat: 28] ﴿Those who disbelieve say: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray, from the jinn and humans, and we will put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest."﴾ [Fussilat: 29] ﴿Indeed, those who say: "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them: "Do not fear and do not grieve, but rejoice in the Garden which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30] ﴿We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. For you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for.﴾ [Fussilat: 31] ﴿As a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful. And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says: "I am among the Muslims"?﴾ [Fussilat: 32] ﴿Good and evil are not equal. Repel evil with what is better, and then the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as if he were a devoted friend.﴾ [Fussilat: 34] ﴿None is granted this except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ [Fussilat: 35] ﴿And if a provocation from Satan provokes you, seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [Fussilat: 36] ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him that you worship.﴾ [Fussilat: 37] ﴿But if they are arrogant, those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they never tire.﴾ [Fussilat: 38] ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, the One who gave it life is the One who gives life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things capable.﴾ [Fussilat: 39] ﴿Indeed, those who distort Our signs are not hidden from Us. Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do what you wish; indeed, He sees what you do.﴾ [Fussilat: 40] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them. And indeed, it is a mighty Book.﴾ [Fussilat: 41] ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.﴾ [Fussilat: 42] ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is One of forgiveness and of painful punishment.﴾ [Fussilat: 43] ﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said: "Why are its verses not made clear? Is it non-Arabic while the messenger is Arab?" Say: "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. But for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. Those are called from a far place."﴾ [Fussilat: 44] (p. 481) ﴿And We gave Moses the Book, but it was disputed. Had a word from your Lord not preceded, the matter would have been decided between them. And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it.﴾ [Fussilat: 45] ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is against it. And your Lord is not unjust to the servants.﴾ [Fussilat: 46] ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. No fruit comes out of its sheaths, no female conceives or gives birth, except with His knowledge. On the day He calls to them: "Where are My partners?" they will say: "We inform You that none of us is a witness."﴾ [Fussilat: 47] ﴿And what they used to invoke before has strayed from them, and they will think that they have no place of refuge.﴾ [Fussilat: 48] ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is hopeless and despairing.﴾ [Fussilat: 49] ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some hardship has touched him, he will say: "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will come. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him." We will certainly inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will certainly make them taste a severe punishment.﴾ [Fussilat: 50] ﴿And when We bestow favour on man, he turns away and withdraws to one side, but when evil touches him, he has long prayers.﴾ [Fussilat: 51] ﴿Say: "Have you considered? If it is from Allah and you then disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?"﴾ [Fussilat: 52] ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient that your Lord is a witness over all things?﴾ [Fussilat: 53] ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about meeting their Lord. Unquestionably, He encompasses all things.﴾ [Fussilat: 54]

Al-Sarsar (the cold wind that burns as fire does), said al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj; the views of the exegetes on it will come.

Al-Nahs (ill-omened): the opposite of good fortune. The poet said:
"It is all the same to him at whatever time you come to him, whether it is an hour of ill-omen to be avoided or of good fortune."

al-Farra' recited:
"Tell Judham and Lakhm that their brothers, Tayy and Bahra', are a people whose help is ill-omened."

Al-Taqyid (pl. al-taqyid): the preparing and facilitating of a thing. "These are two garments of equal value (qayyidan)" when they are equal in price. "Qayidni with this garment" means: take it and give me in exchange its equivalent. Al-muqayada means exchange.

Al-akmam: its singular is kumm. al-Zamakhshari said it is with a kasra on the kaf. al-Mubarrad said it is what covers the fruit before the spathe dries. Whoever says in the plural akimma, its singular is kimam. Al-afaq (the horizons): the regions, its singular is ufuq. The poet said:
"Even if a living being attained, by a station in this world, the horizon of the sky, his hand would attain the horizon."

Ha Mim. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are made distinct... [The Qur'anic verses in this opening section are repeated in the source; they are rendered above.]

This surah is Meccan without disagreement. Its connection to what precedes it: He said at the end of the previous surah: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth?﴾ [Ghafir: 82] to the end. So it included a threat, a warning, and a rebuke to Quraysh. He then followed that rebuke, reproof, and threat with another reproof. He mentioned that He sent down a Book whose verses are detailed, a bearer of good news to whoever follows it and a warner to whoever turns away from it, and that most of Quraysh turned away from it.

Then He mentioned the power of God to create the upper and lower worlds. Then He said: ﴿If they turn away, say: "I have warned you of a thunderbolt"﴾ [Fussilat: 13]. All of this fits the end of Surat al-Mu'min regarding the non-benefit to the deniers of the messengers when punishment overtook them. Likewise, Quraysh suffered what befell its chieftains of killing, capture, plunder, and captivity, and the uprooting of the enemies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), similar to what befell 'Ad and Thamud of uprooting.

It is narrated that 'Utba ibn Rabi'a went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in order to magnify for him the matter of his opposition to his people, to disparage what he had brought, and to make it seem remote. When 'Utba spoke, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: Ha Mim, and went on with it at its beginning until he reached His saying: ﴿If they turn away, say: "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud."﴾ [Fussilat: 13]. The old man trembled and his hair stood on end. He put his hand over the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and appealed to him by the ties of kinship to stop. When he left him, he said: "By Allah, I have heard something that is neither poetry, nor sorcery, nor soothsaying. And I thought that the thunderbolt of punishment was over my head."

"Tanzil" (a revelation) is in the nominative because it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "This is a revelation," according to al-Farra'. Or it is the subject whose predicate is "a Book whose verses are made distinct," according to al-Zajjaj and al-Hawfi. The predicate of "Ha Mim" is if it is the name of the surah. "A Book" according to al-Zajjaj is an apposition to "tanzil." It was said: or a predicate after a predicate.

"Whose verses are made distinct": al-Suddi said: its verses were clarified, meaning its meanings were explained, so its lawful and unlawful, its prohibitions and commands, its promises and threats were differentiated.

It was said: it was made distinct in the revelation, meaning it was not sent down all at once. al-Hasan said: with promise and threat. Sufyan said: with reward and punishment. Ibn Zayd said: distinguishing between Muhammad (ﷺ) and whoever opposes him. It was said: it was made distinct by its sections and by the varieties of the endings of verses, and it did not follow a rhyme or the like, as poetry and rhymed prose do.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: its verses were distinguished and made into detailed meanings of different kinds. Some of them concern the description of the essence of Allah, the explanation of the attributes of transcendence and sanctity, the explanation of the perfection of His knowledge, power, mercy, and wisdom, and the wonders of the states of His creation: the heavens, the stars, the alternation of night and day, and the wonders of the states of plants, animals, and humans. Some of them concern the states of obligations directed toward the heart and toward the limbs. Some concern promise and threat, reward and punishment, and the ranks of the people of Paradise and the depths of the people of Hell. Some concern admonitions and advice. Some concern the refinement of morals and the discipline of the soul. Some concern the stories of earlier peoples and the histories of those who passed away.

Ultimately, whoever is fair will know that at the beginning of creation there was no book that gathered together the diverse sciences and subjects as the Qur'an does. End of quotation.

It is also recited as (fa-ṣalat), with the fa vowelled and the ṣad light (mukhaffafa), meaning: it distinguished between truth and falsehood; or some of its parts were distinguished from others by the difference of its meanings, from the verse ﴿فَصَلَتِ العِيرُ﴾ [Yusuf: 94], i.e., departed (infaṣalat), and "faṣala min al-balad," i.e., he departed from the town. (Qur'anan) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl) in itself, and it is emphatic (mu'akkida), because it does not change; or it is a preparation (tawṭi'a) for the state after it, which is (ʿarabiyyan); or it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar), i.e., he recites it as an Arabic Qur'an; or it is in the accusative for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) and praise (madḥ).

As for the one who makes it a state, it is said that the one in state is (āyātuhu), and it is said (kitāb), because it is described by the words ﴿فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ﴾; or by supposing a hidden verb whose estimate is: "We distinguished it as a Qur'an"; or it is a second object of (fuṣṣilat). These are six opinions, the last of which belongs to al-Akhfash. (Li-qawmin) is connected to (fuṣṣilat), i.e., they know things and understand the proofs, so it is as if it was distinguished for these people, since they benefit from it; they are singled out for mention as an honour. Whoever does not benefit from the distinction is as if it was not distinguished for him. It is unlikely that it is connected to (tanzīl), because it has been described in one of its two connections, if ﴿مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ is in the position of a description, or (kitāb) is substituted from it, or it is the predicate of (tanzīl), in which case there would be a substitution from the relative pronoun and an information about it before it takes its connection, and this is not permissible. It is also said that (li-qawmin) is in the position of a description of (ʿarabiyyan), i.e., existing for a people who know its words and verify that it has not departed from the pattern of their speech; and this is as if it were a refutation of those who claim that there is in the Qur'an what is not from the speech of the Arabs. (Bashīran wa-nadhīran) is in the accusative as a description of ﴿قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾. It is also said it is a state from (āyātuhu). Zayd ibn ʿAlī recited ﴿بَشِيرٌ ونَذِيرٌ﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 19] with both in the nominative, as a description of (kitāb), or as the predicate of an omitted subject. Its good tidings are of Paradise for whoever believes, and its warning is of the Fire for whoever disbelieves.

﴿فَأعْرَضَ أكْثَرُهُمْ﴾: i.e., most of those people; that is, they were among the people of knowledge, but they did not consider it with complete reflection; rather they turned away. ﴿فَهم لا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾: because of their turning away from what it contains of proofs and evidences; or, since it did not benefit them and they did not accept it, they were treated as if they had not heard it.

Then God, exalted is He, informed about them with the statement that indicates the impossibility of their hearts (returning) and of people returning to Him, and of their hearing what follows it; and it is His saying, exalted is He, quoting them: ﴿وقالُوا قُلُوبُنا في أكِنَّةٍ مِمّا تَدْعُونا إلَيْهِ وفي آذانِنا وقْرٌ﴾. The discussion of the like of this has already passed in al-An'am.

Ṭalḥa recited (wiqr) with a kasra on the waw. These are images of the impossibility of accepting the truth, as if their hearts were in a covering, as they said: ﴿وقالُوا قُلُوبُنا غُلْفٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 88], and as if their ears, when the speech of God is mentioned, were deaf. The (ḥijāb) is the veil that prevents response, and it is a difference in religion, because he worships God while they worship idols; this is the meaning stated by al-Farra' and others.

It is narrated that Abu Jahl wrapped a garment over his head and said: "O Muhammad, between us and you is a veil," mocking him. It is said it is an image of non-response. It is said it is an expression for enmity. The (min) in ﴿مِمّا تَدْعُونا إلَيْهِ﴾ is for the beginning of the limit, and likewise in ﴿ومِن بَيْنِنا﴾. The meaning is that the veil began from us and began from you, so the intermediate distance between our direction and your direction is filled with the veil, with no empty space in it. Had he not used (min), the meaning would be that a veil exists midway between the two directions; and the intent is to emphasise extreme separation, which is why (min) was used.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you say: why was it not said, 'upon our hearts are coverings,' as it was said, 'and in our ears is deafness,' so that the speech would be in one pattern?" (I say): It is in one pattern, because there is no difference in meaning between your saying "our hearts are in coverings," and the proof of this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. If it were said, "We have made their hearts in coverings," the meaning would not differ. You see that the obedient ones among them do not observe correspondence and considered metaphor except in meanings, and you say that (fī) is more eloquent in this position than (ʿalā), because they intended the extreme of non-acceptance, since their hearts are in coverings which enclose them in the way a container encloses what is in it, so nothing can reach them. Just as you say: "the money is in the bag," in contrast to "upon the money is a bag," which does not indicate confinement and non-attainment in the way a container does. As for His saying, "We have made," it is information from God, exalted is He, and needs no exaggeration, unlike their saying.

Al-Zamakhshari's saying "you see the obedient ones" means among the Arabs and their poets. For this reason people spoke about the poetry of Habib, and some did not approve of the excessive craft of badi' in it; they said: the best of it is what comes without artifice.

﴿فاعْمَلْ إنَّنا عامِلُونَ﴾. Al-Kalbi said: "Work for our destruction, for we are working for your destruction."

Muqatil said: "Work for your god who sent you, for we are working for our gods whom we worship." Al-Farra' said: "Work according to the requirement of your religion, and we work according to the requirement of our religion." Al-Mawardi mentioned: "Work for your afterlife, for we work for our worldly life."

Since the heart is the locus of knowledge, and hearing and sight are aids in acquiring knowledge, they mentioned that these three are veiled from anything that the Messenger brings reaching them. The saying "So work, for we are working" may mean: you will be wholly abandoned, and it may be contemptuous mockery.

(Qul innamā yūḥā ilayya): The majority recited (qul) in the imperative; Ibn Wathhab and al-A'mash recited (qāla) as a past verb. This is a proclamation of monotheism and prophethood. Al-Nakha'i and al-A'mash recited (yūḥī) with a kasra on the ḥā'; the majority with a fatḥa. He informed that he is a human like them, not an angel, but it was revealed to him rather than to them.

Al-Hasan said: God taught him humility, and that what was revealed to him was the oneness of God and the rejection of your gods.

﴿فاسْتَقِيمُوا إلَيْهِ﴾: i.e., go straight toward Him with monotheism, which is the foundation of religion and of action. ﴿واسْتَغْفِرُوهُ﴾: ask Him for forgiveness, for it is the foundation of action, by whose attainment consequences are removed.

(Istaqīmū) has been given the meaning of turning, which is why it takes (ilā); i.e., direct your uprightness toward Him. Since reason affirms that happiness is tied to two matters: exalting God and compassion toward His creation, He mentioned that woe, perdition and grief are for the polytheists who did not exalt God in His monotheism and the denial of a partner, and did not show compassion to His creation by bringing good to them; and in addition to this they denied resurrection.

The apparent meaning is that (zakāt) is in its literal sense of the zakāt of wealth; this was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib, who said: they used to perform Hajj and ʿUmra but did not pay zakāt. Al-Hasan and Qatada said, and it was said: Quraysh used to feed pilgrims and deprive those among them who believed.

Al-Hasan and Qatada also said: the meaning is that they do not believe in zakāt and do not acknowledge it.

Mujahid and al-Rabi' said: they do not purify their deeds. Ibn ʿAbbas and the majority said: zakāt here is "There is no god but God," monotheism, as Musa, peace be upon him, said to Pharaoh: ﴿هَلْ لَكَ إلى أنْ تَزَكّى﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 18]. What supports this interpretation is that the verse is from the early Meccan period, and the zakāt of wealth was revealed in Medina; this was said by Ibn ʿAtiyya, who said: this is only the zakāt of the heart and body, i.e., purification from polytheism and sins; and Mujahid and al-Rabi' said the same.

Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: zakāt here is spending in obedience. End of quotation.

If the zakāt intended is the giving of wealth, then it was linked with disbelief because it is burdensome to give away wealth, which is beloved to human nature and the brother of the soul, as an incitement to it. A certain man of letters said:

They said: "The soul's brother is your wealth, so guard it." I replied: "Wealth is better than the soul."
I see that guarding it leads to the improvement of my condition, and squandering it leads to a shameful begging.

﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning the sick and the infirm who are unable to complete acts of obedience; for them is written a reward like the best of what they used to do. (Mamnūn) means diminished; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with him. Dhu al-Asbagh al-ʿAdwani said:

By your life, my door is not locked against a friend, nor is my goodness diminished.

Mujahid said: "not counted." It is also said: "not cut off." The poet said:

The bounty of the generous over the slow horses; he gives in that way neither diminished nor hasty.

It is also said: he does not reproach with it, because God's gifts are an honour, whereas reproach only enters human gifts. It is also said: he does not reproach with it, because it is only a reproach of favour; as for the other (the reward), it is a right whose payment is owed. Al-Zamakhshari transmitted this, and in it there is a hint of Mu'tazilite doctrine.

﴿قُلْ أئِنَّكم لَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾: a question of rebuke and reproach against them, for disbelieving in the One who brought into being the world, its lower and upper parts, and described the form of its creation and its duration; and the wisdom in creating over a period of time while He is capable of bringing it into being all at once.

So God mentioned the bringing into being of these things in sequence, and the discussion of what was first begun in creation and what was created in sequence has already passed.

The meaning of ﴿فِي يَوْمَيْنِ﴾ is: within the measure of two days.

﴿وتَجْعَلُونَ لَهُ أنْدادًا﴾: i.e., likenesses and equals from among the angels, the jinn and the idols, which they worship besides Him. al-Suddi said: equals among men whom they obey.

(Wa-tajʿalūna) is conjoined to ﴿لَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾, so it falls within the scope of the interrogation that implies denial and rebuke. (Dhālika): i.e., the Originator of the earth and its Inventor, ﴿رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾, is (distinct) from the equals you have set up for Him and others.

﴿وجَعَلَ فِيها رَواسِيَ﴾: a new statement, not part of the relative clause at all; rather it is conjoined to His saying ﴿لَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾.

﴿وبارَكَ فِيها﴾: He multiplied its good within it.

﴿وقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها﴾: i.e., the provisions of its inhabitants and their livelihoods; and He attributed both to the earth in terms of their being in it and emerging from it; this was said by al-Suddi.

Qatada said: "its sustenance" means from the mountains, rivers, trees, rocks, minerals, and the things by which the earth's stability and benefits subsist.

Mujahid said: "its sustenance" means from the rain and waters. ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak and Mujahid also said: its specific properties which He distributed among the lands, by which each region is distinguished, so that some of them need others for sustenance through clothing, food and plants.

﴿فِي أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ﴾: i.e., in the full completion of four days, together with the two days mentioned earlier. Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿فِي أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ﴾ is for the duration of God's creation and what is in it, as if He said: all of that was in four complete days, equal, without addition or subtraction.

Al-Zajjaj said: "in completion of four days," meaning by the completion the two days. End of quotation. This is like saying: "I built the wall of my house in one day, and completed all of it in two days," meaning with the first.

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Razi said: From al-Zamakhshari's words one understands an additional benefit in ﴿فِي أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ﴾ beyond His saying "in two days," because "in two days" does not imply that the work was entirely occupied with that. But when He mentioned the creation of the earth and the creation of these things, then said ﴿فِي أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ سَواءً﴾, this indicates that these days were fully occupied with those works without addition or subtraction. End of quotation.

﴿in four days﴾ is not different from ﴿two days and four days﴾ in terms of encompassing (istighraq, the sense of covering the whole span). If ﴿four﴾ implies encompassing, then so do the two days. When a counted time-span is mentioned, the verb applies to all of it, either generally, as in "I traveled two days," or to part of each day, as in "I prayed at night for two nights." Encompassing is therefore possible, and so is partial occurrence within each of the two nights. In the same way, the creation of the earth could have occurred during part of each of the two days, or the two days could have been wholly devoted to it. Likewise, ﴿in four days﴾ allows for encompassing, and the creation of the earth, the mountains, the blessing, and the apportioning of its sustenance could have occurred during part of each of the four days [p-486]. Thus, what Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said adds no further benefit.

Al-Jumhur read (سَواءً) with the accusative (naṣb) as a circumstantial state (ḥāl). Abu Ja'far read it with the nominative (raf'), meaning "it is equal." Zayd ibn 'Ali, al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd, 'Isa, and Ya'qub read it with the genitive (khafḍ), as an adjective (na't) of ﴿four days﴾.
